exams.name: Civil Services Examination
exams.fullName: UPSC Civil Services Examination — IAS, IPS, IFS(F) & 20+ Group A/B services
exams.about: India's flagship exam. One screening Prelims paper set, nine descriptive Mains papers and a personality test decide your rank — and the service you get.
exams.eligibility: Graduation in any discipline from a recognised university (final-year students may apply for Prelims). Age 21–32 years for General/EWS on 1 August of the exam year, with relaxation for OBC, SC/ST, PwBD and ex-servicemen.
exams.attempts: 6 attempts for General/EWS, 9 for OBC, unlimited for SC/ST — always within the age limit.

stages.name: Prelims
stages.note: Screening only — marks are NOT added to the final rank. CSAT is qualifying at 33% for General category.

stages.name: Mains
stages.note: Nine papers over five days. Essay, GS I–IV and the two Optional papers (250 each = 1750) form the merit; the two language papers are qualifying at 25%.

stages.name: Personality Test
stages.note: Final merit = Mains 1750 + Interview 275 = 2025 marks. The DAF drives most questions.

syllabus.subject: GS Paper I — Prelims
topics: History of India: Ancient, Medieval and Modern
Indian Polity: Constitution, governance, Panchayati Raj
Geography of India and the world

syllabus.subject: Essay
topics: Two essays of ~250 words each from Section A and Section B
Indian examples, data and constitutional angles

syllabus.subject: GS Paper I
topics: Indian culture — literature, architecture, art forms
Modern Indian history from the mid-18th century
Indian society: diversity, women, population, globalisation
Physical and human geography, resources, disasters

syllabus.subject: GS Paper II
topics: Union and State functions, federal issues
Judiciary, tribunals, constitutional and statutory bodies
Social justice, welfare schemes, health and education

syllabus.subject: GS Paper III
topics: Science and technology in everyday life
Internal security, cyber security, money laundering

syllabus.subject: GS Paper IV — Ethics
topics: Ethics and human interface, moral values
Contributions of moral thinkers — Indian and world
Public service values, Codes of Conduct and Citizen's Charter
Case studies: service delivery, crisis, conflict of interest

syllabus.subject: Optional Subject (2 papers)
topics: Paper I and Paper II of 250 marks each
High-scoring picks: PSIR, Sociology, Geography, Anthropology
Others: History, Public Administration, Law, Literature, Maths
Overlap with GS keeps the load realistic

syllabus.subject: Qualifying Language Papers
topics: Paper A — one Indian language from the 8th Schedule
Qualifying at 25% each; marks are not counted in the merit

timeline.label: Annual calendar
timeline.note: UPSC fixes Prelims and Mains dates for the next cycle here.

timeline.label: CSE notification
timeline.note: Vacancy count and the application link go live on upsc.gov.in.

timeline.label: Application window
timeline.note: Online form plus the One Time Registration (OTR) profile.

timeline.label: Prelims admit card
timeline.note: Released ~2 weeks before the exam.

timeline.label: Prelims
timeline.note: GS I in the morning, CSAT in the afternoon — same day.

timeline.label: Mains
timeline.note: Essay and GS I–IV on the first three days, language papers after a break.

timeline.label: Personality test
timeline.window: February – April of the next year
timeline.note: Board interview in Delhi; travel is reimbursed.

timeline.label: Final result & service allotment
timeline.window: April – May of the next year
timeline.note: Rank list drives service and cadre allocation.

exams.name: Engineering Services Examination (IES)
exams.fullName: UPSC Engineering Services Examination — IES officers in Railways, CPWD, Telecom, Defence Works and PSUs
exams.about: The technical arm of UPSC. Four engineering disciplines compete for Group A engineering services — objective Prelims, conventional Mains and an interview.
exams.eligibility: B.E./B.Tech (or equivalent) in the relevant discipline, or an AMIE/Section A&B pass. Age 21–30 years for General, with the usual relaxations.
exams.attempts: Unlimited within the age limit.
exams.mode: Offline (OMR for Prelims, pen & paper for Mains)

stages.name: Prelims
stages.note: Two papers the same day; only 25% of Prelims marks are carried forward.

stages.name: Mains
stages.note: Two discipline papers of 300 marks each, 3 hours each.

stages.name: Personality Test
stages.note: Total = Prelims carry-forward (25%) + Mains + Interview.

syllabus.subject: GS & Engineering Aptitude
topics: Safety, health and environment in engineering works
Standards, quality and Indian engineering initiatives

syllabus.subject: Civil Engineering discipline
topics: Structural engineering, RCC and steel design

syllabus.subject: Mechanical Engineering discipline
topics: Thermodynamics, power plants and IC engines
Theory of machines, design of machine elements

syllabus.subject: Electronics & Telecom discipline
topics: Electronic devices, analog and digital circuits

exams.name: National Defence Academy & Naval Academy Examination
exams.fullName: UPSC NDA & NA (I/II) — Army, Navy, Air Force and Naval Academy wings after Class 12
exams.about: Entry into the NDA right after Class 12. Two written papers, then a five-day SSB that is worth as much as the written test itself.
exams.eligibility: Unmarried candidates aged 16.5–19.5 years. Class 12 pass (or appearing) — Physics and Maths compulsory for the Navy and Air Force wings.
exams.attempts: Limited only by the age window; both NDA (I) and NDA (II) cycles are open each year.

stages.name: Mathematics
stages.note: Class 12 level; speed and accuracy decide the cut-off.

stages.name: General Ability Test
stages.note: Part A English (200 marks) + Part B General Knowledge (400 marks).

sections.name: Part B — History, Geography & current events

stages.name: SSB Interview
stages.mode: Selection centres: Allahabad, Bhopal, Bangalore, Kapurthala, Mysuru
stages.note: Stage I screening (OIR + PPDT), Stage II psychology tests, GTO tasks and the personal interview over 5 days.

syllabus.subject: Mathematics
topics: Algebra: sets, complex numbers, quadratic equations, sequences

syllabus.subject: General Ability — GK
topics: Physics: mechanics, heat, optics, electricity, modern physics
Chemistry: elements, acids & bases, metals, carbon compounds
History of India and the freedom movement
Current events, defence news and important personalities

syllabus.subject: SSB — psychology & GTO
topics: GTO: group discussion, obstacle race, command task, lecturette
Personal interview based on the PIQ form
Physical fitness, sports and confidence drills

timeline.label: SSB interviews
timeline.window: Rolling — 4 to 6 months after each written result
timeline.note: Five-day board at your chosen SSB centre.

exams.name: Combined Defence Services Examination
exams.fullName: UPSC CDS (I/II) — IMA, INA, AFA and Officers' Training Academy for graduates
exams.about: Graduate entry into the armed forces. English, General Knowledge and Elementary Mathematics on the written side, then the same SSB that decides everything.
exams.eligibility: Degree for IMA/OTA; Engineering degree for INA and AFA (Physics + Maths at 12th for AFA). Age limits differ per academy (roughly 19–25 years).
exams.attempts: Within the age limit; two cycles every year.

stages.name: Elementary Mathematics
stages.note: Not applicable for OTA candidates — they write English and GK only.

stages.name: SSB Interview
stages.note: 300 marks for IMA/INA/AFA, 200 for OTA.

syllabus.subject: English
topics: Cloze test and fill in the blanks

syllabus.subject: General Knowledge
topics: History of India and the freedom struggle

syllabus.subject: Elementary Mathematics
topics: Arithmetic: percentages, ratio, average, time & work

syllabus.subject: SSB preparation
topics: GTO tasks: GD, GPE, half group, command task

exams.name: Bihar Combined Competitive Examination
exams.fullName: BPSC Combined Competitive Exam — Bihar Administrative Service, Deputy SP & state Group A/B posts
exams.about: Bihar's own civil services cycle: a single objective Prelims, a five-paper Mains with a strong Bihar-specific tilt, and a 120-mark interview.
exams.eligibility: Graduation in any discipline from a recognised university. Minimum age 20–22 years; upper age 37 years for male General candidates with relaxation for women, BC/EBC and reserved categories as per Bihar rules.
exams.attempts: No cap — you can appear every year inside the age limit.

stages.name: Prelims
stages.note: One General Studies paper. Purely a screening test — Prelims marks are not added to the final merit.

stages.name: Mains
stages.note: GS Paper I, GS Paper II and Essay (300 each = 900) form the merit. General Hindi (100) and the Optional (100, objective) are qualifying.

stages.name: Interview / Personality Test
stages.note: Final merit = 900 (Mains) + 120 (Interview) = 1020 marks.

syllabus.subject: Prelims — General Studies
topics: History of India with special reference to Bihar
Geography of India and Bihar: rivers, districts, resources
Indian polity, Panchayati Raj and community development
Indian economy and the economy of Bihar
Current affairs — national, international and Bihar-specific
General mental ability, basic numeracy and data interpretation

syllabus.subject: GS Paper I
topics: Modern history of India, with Bihar's role highlighted
Indian National Movement and Bihar's contribution
Statistical analysis: graphs, diagrams and data interpretation

syllabus.subject: GS Paper II
topics: Indian polity and Bihar's political system
Indian economy, planning and the Bihar economy
Geography of India with a Bihar focus
Role of science and technology in development
Environment, disaster management and Bihar's schemes

syllabus.subject: Essay
topics: Two essays on social, economic and Bihar-specific themes
Data, examples and Bihar case studies

syllabus.subject: Optional Subject (objective)
topics: Choose one: History, Geography, Political Science, Sociology
Economics, Public Administration, Law, Labour & Welfare

syllabus.subject: Interview
topics: Bihar current affairs and state government schemes

timeline.label: Annual calendar
timeline.note: BPSC now publishes a fixed yearly calendar for CCE and the TRE posts.

timeline.label: Application window
timeline.note: Online form on bpsc.bih.nic.in with a short correction window.

timeline.label: Prelims
timeline.note: 150 MCQs, 2 hours, 1/3 negative marking.

timeline.label: Mains
timeline.note: General Hindi, GS I, GS II, Essay and the objective Optional.

timeline.label: Interview
timeline.note: Held at BPSC, Patna.

exams.name: State Civil Services (common pattern)
exams.fullName: UPPSC · MPPSC · RPSC (RAS) · WBPSC · MPSC · APPSC · TNPSC · KPSC · HPSC
exams.body: The respective State Public Service Commissions
exams.about: Most state PSCs repeat UPSC's shape with a state twist: an objective screening Prelims, descriptive GS Mains (plus a state-language or optional paper) and an interview. The state GK block is what actually decides ranks.
exams.eligibility: Graduation in any discipline; state domicile rules, age limits and relaxations differ per commission.
exams.attempts: Varies — UPPSC and MPPSC cap attempts by category, many states have no cap inside the age limit.
exams.mode: Offline (some states have moved Prelims to CBT)

stages.name: Prelims
stages.note: One or two GS papers; screening only.

stages.name: Mains
stages.note: Usually GS Paper I + GS Paper II (200 each) and an Essay or state-language paper.

stages.name: Interview
stages.note: 100–150 marks depending on the state.

syllabus.subject: State-specific GK
topics: State history, dynasties and freedom struggle
State geography: rivers, soil, minerals, districts
Culture, festivals, tribes, literature and dance forms
State economy, budget and flagship schemes
State polity: Panchayati Raj, urban bodies, state acts

syllabus.subject: History & Culture of India
topics: Modern India and the national movement

syllabus.subject: Science, Environment & Current Affairs
topics: General science and technology in daily life
State current affairs and government orders

timeline.label: Notification
timeline.note: Each commission announces its own cycle; UPPSC and MPPSC usually start the year.

exams.name: Combined Graduate Level Examination
exams.fullName: SSC CGL — Assistant Section Officer, Income Tax Inspector, CBI, Auditor, JSO and 20+ Group B/C posts
exams.about: The highest-volume graduate recruitment in India. Tier 1 is a 60-minute speed test; Tier 2 is where the rank is actually built.
exams.eligibility: Bachelor's degree from a recognised university. Age 18–32 years for most posts (post-wise relaxation applies).
exams.attempts: No limit inside the age window.

stages.name: Tier 1
stages.note: Qualifying only — Tier 2 decides the merit.

stages.name: Tier 2 — Paper 1
stages.negative: 1 mark per wrong answer (Sections I & II)
stages.note: Compulsory for every post; DEST (data entry speed test) is qualifying.

stages.name: Document verification & medical
stages.note: Original documents, physical standards (for CBI/excise posts) and medical test.

syllabus.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
topics: Percentage, profit & loss, ratio and proportion
Data interpretation: tables, pie charts, bar graphs

syllabus.subject: Reasoning & General Intelligence
topics: Non-verbal: mirror image, paper folding, embedded figures

syllabus.subject: English Language
topics: Fill in the blanks, idioms and one-word substitution

syllabus.subject: General Awareness
topics: Indian history, polity and the Constitution
Geography of India and the world
Static GK: books, awards, sports, days

syllabus.subject: Computer Knowledge
topics: Shortcuts, number systems and DBMS basics

syllabus.subject: Statistics (JSO posts)
topics: Measures of central tendency and dispersion

syllabus.subject: Typing (DEST)
topics: Data Entry Speed Test on a passage
Qualifying only — but a failure here costs the post

timeline.label: Application window
timeline.note: One-time registration (OTR) is now mandatory.

timeline.label: Tier 1
timeline.note: Multi-shift CBT over ~2 weeks.

exams.name: Combined Higher Secondary Level Examination
exams.fullName: SSC CHSL — LDC, JSA and Data Entry Operator posts in ministries and departments
exams.about: The Class 12 gateway to central government clerical posts. A speed-based Tier 1, a longer Tier 2 and a typing/skill test decide the final list.
exams.eligibility: Class 12 pass from a recognised board. Age 18–27 years (post-wise relaxation).
exams.attempts: No limit inside the age window.

stages.name: Tier 2 — Session I
stages.negative: 1 mark per wrong answer (Maths & Reasoning sections)

stages.name: Tier 2 — Session II
stages.note: Typing test (35 wpm English / 30 wpm Hindi) for LDC-JSA; skill test for DEO.

syllabus.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
topics: Time & work, time & distance, boats and streams

syllabus.subject: Reasoning
topics: Blood relations, direction sense and ranking

syllabus.subject: General Awareness
topics: Current affairs of the last year
History, polity, geography and economy basics

syllabus.subject: Typing / skill
topics: Speed and accuracy on a printed passage
Qualifying but decisive — many candidates lose the post here

exams.name: Non-Technical Popular Categories
exams.fullName: RRB NTPC — Station Master, Goods Guard, Junior Clerk, Commercial Clerk, Trains Clerk
exams.body: Railway Recruitment Boards (RRB), Ministry of Railways
exams.about: The railways' graduate and Class-12 level recruitment. Two CBTs, then typing/CBAT depending on the post, then document verification and medical.
exams.eligibility: Class 12 or graduation depending on the post. Age 18–33 years (relaxation as per rules).
exams.attempts: No limit inside the age window.

stages.name: CBT 1
stages.note: Screening — normalised marks are used only to shortlist for CBT 2.

stages.name: Typing skill test / CBAT
stages.note: Typing for clerk posts, CBAT (psycho test) for Station Master and Goods Guard.

stages.name: Document verification & medical
stages.note: A2/A3 medical standards apply for safety categories.

syllabus.subject: Mathematics
topics: Percentage, profit & loss, simple and compound interest

syllabus.subject: General Awareness
topics: Indian history, culture and freedom struggle
Geography of India and the world

timeline.label: Notification
timeline.note: Published zone-wise on the RRB portals.

exams.name: Level 1 (Group D) Recruitment
exams.fullName: RRB Group D / Level 1 — Track Maintainer, Assistant Pointsman, Hospital Attendant and Workshop posts
exams.about: The largest single recruitment in the country. One CBT, a physical efficiency test and medical decide the list — no interview.
exams.eligibility: Class 10 pass (or ITI/NAC in a trade for some posts). Age 18–36 years.
exams.attempts: No limit inside the age window.

stages.name: Physical Efficiency Test
stages.note: Male: 30 kg over 100 m in 2 minutes + 1000 m run in 4:15. Female: 20 kg over 100 m + 1000 m in 5:40.

stages.name: Document verification & medical
stages.note: A-2 / A-3 vision and fitness standards.

syllabus.subject: General Science
topics: Physics — motion, force, work, energy, sound, light
Chemistry — matter, acids & bases, metals, carbon

syllabus.subject: General Awareness & Current Affairs
topics: Current affairs of the last 6–12 months
Indian geography, history and polity basics

exams.name: Probationary Officer (CRP PO/MT)
exams.fullName: IBPS PO/MT — Probationary Officer in 11 public sector banks
exams.about: A 60-minute Prelims, a 3-hour Mains with a descriptive English paper, and then the interview. Speed in Prelims, depth in Mains.
exams.eligibility: Graduation in any discipline. Age 20–30 years (relaxation for reserved categories).
exams.attempts: No limit inside the age window.

stages.name: Prelims
stages.note: Sectional timing of 20 minutes per section; qualifying only.

stages.name: Mains — objective
stages.note: Sectional timing applies.

stages.name: Mains — descriptive
stages.note: One letter and one essay typed on the keyboard.

stages.name: Interview
stages.note: Final merit = Mains 225 + Interview 100, then scaled to 80:20.

syllabus.subject: English Language
topics: Error spotting, sentence correction and improvement
Cloze test, fillers and para jumbles
Descriptive: formal letter and essay structure

syllabus.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
topics: Time & work, time & distance, boats and streams

syllabus.subject: Reasoning Ability
topics: Puzzles: floor, box, linear and circular seating

syllabus.subject: Banking, Economy & GA
topics: Banking awareness, RBI circulars and financial terms

syllabus.subject: Interview
topics: Banking awareness and current economic issues

timeline.label: IBPS annual calendar
timeline.note: IBPS publishes the whole year's exam schedule up front.

exams.name: Clerical Cadre (CRP CSA)
exams.fullName: IBPS Clerk / CRP CSA — Clerical cadre in 11 public sector banks
exams.about: The clerical counterpart of the PO cycle: Prelims and Mains only, no interview — so the Mains score is the entire merit.
exams.eligibility: Graduation in any discipline. Age 20–28 years. Local language proficiency of the applying state is mandatory.
exams.attempts: No limit inside the age window.

stages.name: Prelims
stages.note: 20 minutes per section.

stages.name: Language Proficiency Test
stages.note: Conducted by the participating bank before joining.

syllabus.subject: Numerical / Quantitative Aptitude
topics: Profit & loss, simple and compound interest

exams.name: Probationary Officer
exams.fullName: State Bank of India Probationary Officer — India's largest public sector bank
exams.about: Prelims, a Mains with a descriptive English paper, then a Group Exercise and Interview. SBI's Mains is the hardest banking paper in the country.
exams.eligibility: Graduation in any discipline. Age 21–30 years.
exams.attempts: 4 for General, 7 for OBC, unlimited for SC/ST/PwBD within the age limit.

stages.name: Prelims
stages.note: 20 minutes per section.

stages.name: Group Exercise & Interview
stages.note: Final merit = 250 (Mains) + 50 (GE & Interview) = 300.

syllabus.subject: Banking & Financial Awareness
topics: RBI policies, monetary tools and circulars

syllabus.subject: Group Exercise & Interview
topics: Group discussion on current and banking topics
Awareness of SBI's products and digital push

exams.name: Grade B Officer (General / DEPR / DR)
exams.fullName: Reserve Bank of India Grade B Officer — General, DEPR and DR streams
exams.about: The regulator's own officer exam: an objective Phase 1 with tight sectional cut-offs, a Phase 2 that mixes objective and descriptive writing, then an interview.
exams.eligibility: Graduation with 60% (50% for SC/ST/PwBD) or a post-graduation with 55%. Age 21–30 years (relaxation applies).
exams.attempts: 6 attempts for General category in the General stream; no cap for SC/ST/OBC/PwBD within the age limit.

stages.name: Phase 1
stages.note: Sectional cut-offs make this the most filtered stage.

stages.name: Phase 2 — Paper I (ESI)
stages.note: Economic and Social Issues: 50% objective, 50% descriptive.

stages.name: Phase 2 — Paper II (FM)
stages.note: Finance and Management: 50% objective, 50% descriptive.

stages.name: Phase 2 — Paper III (English)
stages.note: Precis, reading comprehension and an essay.

stages.name: Interview
stages.note: Final merit = Phase 2 (300) + Interview (75).

syllabus.subject: Economic & Social Issues (ESI)
topics: Growth, development and Indian economic policy
Inflation, monetary policy and the RBI's role
Fiscal policy, budgeting and public debt
Social structure: poverty, inclusion, health, education

syllabus.subject: Finance & Management (FM)
topics: Financial system: regulators, markets and instruments
Risk management in banking, Basel norms, NPA
Union Budget, primary and secondary markets

syllabus.subject: General Awareness
topics: Current affairs — 4 to 6 months of depth

syllabus.subject: English (descriptive)
topics: Essay on economic and social themes

exams.name: Common Law Admission Test
exams.fullName: CLAT UG — 5-year BA LLB / BBA LLB admission to 24+ National Law Universities
exams.about: One passage-based paper decides your law school. Reading speed and legal reasoning matter far more than memorised law — every principle is given inside the passage.
exams.eligibility: Class 12 pass or appearing with 45% (40% for SC/ST/PwBD). No upper age limit and no cap on attempts.
exams.attempts: Unlimited.

stages.name: CLAT UG
stages.note: Five sections, all built on ~450-word passages. Maximum difficulty is Class 12 level.

stages.name: Counselling
stages.note: All-India counselling by the Consortium; NLU-wise merit lists and choice filling.

syllabus.subject: English Language
topics: Vocabulary in context: synonyms and antonyms
Grammar and sentence correction inside passages

syllabus.subject: Current Affairs & General Knowledge
topics: National and international news of the last 12–18 months

syllabus.subject: Legal Reasoning
topics: Applying the rule given in the passage to new facts
Identifying the principle and its exceptions
Awareness of landmark cases mentioned in the passage

syllabus.subject: Logical Reasoning
topics: Short puzzles, sets and conditional logic

syllabus.subject: Quantitative Techniques
topics: Data interpretation from graphs, tables and passages
Averages, profit & loss and time & work

timeline.label: Notification & syllabus
timeline.note: The Consortium confirms pattern and syllabus for the next edition.

timeline.label: CLAT exam
timeline.note: CLAT 2027 is scheduled for 6 December 2026.

timeline.label: Session begins
timeline.window: June – July of the next year

exams.name: All India Law Entrance Test
exams.fullName: AILET — admission to NLU Delhi (BA LLB Hons, LLM and PhD)
exams.about: NLU Delhi runs its own entrance instead of CLAT. A tighter 90-minute paper with a heavier quant and reasoning share.
exams.eligibility: Class 12 pass or appearing with 50% (45% for SC/ST/PwBD). No age limit.
exams.attempts: Unlimited.

stages.name: Merit list & admission
stages.note: Direct merit list with category-wise seat matrix.

syllabus.subject: Current Affairs & GK
topics: Static GK: history, polity, awards, sports

syllabus.subject: Quantitative Techniques
topics: Arithmetic: percentages, ratio, average, profit & loss

exams.name: Chartered Accountancy
exams.fullName: ICAI Chartered Accountancy — Foundation, Intermediate, Articleship and Final (New Scheme)
exams.body: Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI)
exams.about: India's toughest professional course. Four Foundation papers, six Intermediate papers in two groups, two years of articleship, self-paced online modules and six Final papers. No negative marking in descriptive papers — but the passing bar is 40% per paper and 50% per group.
exams.eligibility: Foundation: Class 12 pass or appearing (register with ICAI Board of Studies). Intermediate: Foundation pass, or direct entry after graduation — 55% for commerce graduates, 60% for others. Final: both Intermediate groups cleared plus articleship and Advanced ICITSS.
exams.attempts: Unlimited; registrations are valid for 10 years and can be revalidated.
exams.mode: Offline (pen & paper) — 70% descriptive, 30% case-based MCQ at Inter and Final

stages.name: Foundation
stages.note: Four papers of 100 marks each, 3 hours each. Two objective papers carry negative marking.

stages.name: ICITSS
stages.note: Integrated Course on Information Technology and Soft Skills — 4 weeks, mandatory before articleship.

stages.name: Articleship
stages.note: 2 years of examination-free practical training. The second year can be industrial training.

stages.name: Self-Paced Online Modules
stages.note: SET A/B and SET C/D must be cleared before the Final exam.

stages.name: Advanced ICITSS
stages.note: Mandatory multi-disciplinary training before the Final.

sections.name: Paper 3 — Advanced Auditing, Assurance & Professional Ethics
Paper 4 — Direct Tax Laws & International Taxation

syllabus.subject: Foundation — Accounting
topics: Theoretical framework, accounting concepts and policies
Company accounts: share capital, debentures, forfeiture

syllabus.subject: Foundation — Quantitative Aptitude
topics: Business mathematics: ratio, percentage, interest, annuity
Logical reasoning: number series, coding, seating
Statistics: measures of central tendency and dispersion

syllabus.subject: Foundation — Business Economics
topics: Public finance and Indian economy basics

syllabus.subject: Inter Paper 1 — Advanced Accounting
topics: Accounting Standards and Ind AS application

syllabus.subject: Inter Paper 2 — Corporate & Other Laws
topics: Companies Act 2013 in full: share capital, meetings, accounts
General laws: contracts, LLP and interpretations

syllabus.subject: Inter Paper 3 — Taxation
topics: Section A — Income Tax: heads of income, clubbing, set-off
Section B — GST: supply, levy, input tax credit

syllabus.subject: Inter Paper 4 — Cost & Management Accounting
topics: Cost sheet, costing systems and job/process costing
Budgeting, budgetary control and decision making

syllabus.subject: Inter Paper 5 — Auditing & Ethics
topics: Audit strategy, risk assessment and internal control
Company audit, audit report and CARO
Audit of banks, NBFCs and PSUs
Professional ethics, quality control and independence

syllabus.subject: Inter Paper 6 — FM & Strategic Management
topics: Time value of money, capital structure and cost of capital
Capital budgeting and working capital management
Organisational design, control and emerging trends

syllabus.subject: Final Paper 1 — Financial Reporting
topics: Ind AS in depth, fair value and financial instruments

syllabus.subject: Final Paper 2 — Advanced Financial Management
topics: Financial policy, capital structure and dividend decisions
Security analysis, portfolio management and CAPM

syllabus.subject: Final Paper 3 — Advanced Auditing & Professional Ethics
topics: Standards on Auditing and quality control
Group audits, forensic audit and internal audit
Audit of banks, insurance companies and NBFCs
Public sector audit, IT audit and data analytics
Professional ethics, misconduct and disciplinary cases

syllabus.subject: Final Paper 4 — Direct Tax & International Taxation
topics: Income tax law in depth: assessments and appeals
Tax planning vs tax avoidance, GAAR
DTAA, non-resident taxation and FEMA overlap
International tax developments and case law

syllabus.subject: Final Paper 5 — Indirect Tax Laws
topics: GST law: supply, valuation, ITC, refunds
Customs law: duty computation, valuation, FTP
Compliance, audits and litigation under GST

syllabus.subject: Final Paper 6 — Integrated Business Solutions
topics: Cross-subject integration: accounts, tax, audit, FM

syllabus.subject: Self-Paced Online Modules (SPOM)
topics: SET A — Foundation of corporate and economic laws
SET B — Advanced constitutional and corporate laws
SET C/D — Strategic cost & performance management, technology
Attempt any time after Intermediate; mandatory before Final

timeline.label: Foundation registration
timeline.note: Register with the Board of Studies, then complete the 4-month study period.

timeline.label: Exam application forms
timeline.note: Forms for the September / November cycle open in early July.

timeline.label: Foundation exam — May cycle
timeline.note: Four papers over about a week.

timeline.label: Intermediate exam — May cycle
timeline.note: Group I and Group II on alternate days.

timeline.label: Results
timeline.window: About 2 to 2.5 months after each cycle
timeline.note: May results in July, September results in November, November results in January.

timeline.label: Articleship
timeline.note: Examination-free practical training under a practising CA.

timeline.label: ICAI membership
timeline.note: Apply for the Certificate of Practice to sign as a CA.

exams.name: Common Admission Test
exams.fullName: CAT — admission to the IIMs and 1,300+ MBA programmes
exams.body: Indian Institutes of Management (one IIM conducts it each year on rotation)
exams.about: Three sections, forty minutes each, and one of the highest percentiles games in Indian education. Accuracy beats attempts because the paper is normalised across slots.
exams.eligibility: Bachelor's degree with 50% (45% for SC/ST/PwBD). Final-year students can apply.
exams.attempts: No cap.

stages.name: CAT
stages.negative: +3 per correct, −1 per wrong MCQ; no penalty for TITA
stages.note: 40 minutes per section — you cannot switch back. Question counts shift slightly each year.

stages.name: WAT / PI rounds
stages.note: Each IIM shortlists separately on its own cut-off and criteria.

syllabus.subject: Data Interpretation & Logical Reasoning
topics: Sets: tables, bar, line, pie, radar and caselets

syllabus.subject: Quantitative Ability
topics: Arithmetic: percentages, ratio, averages, TSD, T&W

timeline.label: Mock test portal
timeline.note: Official section-wise mock with the real interface.

timeline.label: CAT exam
timeline.note: Three slots across the day; you are allotted one.

timeline.label: Result
timeline.note: Scaled scores and percentiles.

exams.name: Joint Entrance Examination — Main
exams.fullName: JEE (Main) — Paper 1 B.E./B.Tech, Paper 2A B.Arch, Paper 2B B.Planning
exams.about: The gateway to NITs, IIITs, GFTIs and the qualifier for JEE Advanced. Two sessions a year and the better NTA score is used, so a bad January is recoverable in April.
exams.eligibility: Class 12 pass or appearing with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics. No age limit; the 75% board criterion depends on the institute.
exams.attempts: 3 consecutive years from the year you pass Class 12.
exams.mode: Computer based test (CBT); the drawing part of B.Arch is pen & paper

stages.name: Paper 1 — B.E./B.Tech
stages.negative: +4 per correct, −1 per wrong MCQ; no penalty for numerical
stages.note: Each subject: Section A (20 MCQ) + Section B (5 numerical value questions).

stages.name: Counselling
stages.note: NTA percentile feeds JoSAA, state CETs and institute lists.

syllabus.subject: Physics
topics: Work, energy, power and rotational motion
Gravitation, properties of solids and fluids
EM induction, alternating current and EM waves
Ray & wave optics, dual nature of matter

syllabus.subject: Chemistry
topics: Physical chemistry: mole concept, atomic structure, states of matter
Coordination compounds, metallurgy and qualitative analysis
Organic: basic principles, hydrocarbons, functional groups
Aldehydes, ketones, acids, amines, biomolecules and polymers

syllabus.subject: Mathematics
topics: Sets, relations, complex numbers and quadratic equations
Indefinite and definite integration, area under curves
Straight lines, circles, parabola, ellipse and hyperbola

exams.name: Joint Entrance Examination — Advanced
exams.fullName: JEE (Advanced) — admission to 23 IITs
exams.body: One IIT on rotation (organized by the Joint Admission Board)
exams.about: Only the top ~2.5 lakh JEE Main qualifiers can sit. Two three-hour papers in one day, with multi-correct, integer and partial-credit questions.
exams.eligibility: Top ~2,50,000 rank holders of JEE Main (Paper 1) of the same year, with Class 12 in PCM. Maximum two attempts in two consecutive years.
exams.attempts: 2 consecutive years.

stages.name: Paper 1
stages.negative: Section-wise: full, partial, zero or negative marks per question type
stages.note: 9:00 AM - 12:00 noon. Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics; question count and marking shift slightly every year.

stages.name: Paper 2
stages.negative: Section-wise: full, partial, zero or negative marks per question type
stages.note: 2:30 PM - 5:30 PM. Same structure as Paper 1; both papers are compulsory and equally weighted (360 marks together).

stages.name: AAT (Architecture Aptitude Test)
stages.note: Qualifying only, for candidates who want B.Arch seats at IIT Kharagpur.

syllabus.subject: Physics
topics: Mechanics: kinematics, Newton's laws, rotation, gravitation
Modern physics: photoelectric effect, atoms, nuclei

syllabus.subject: Chemistry
topics: Physical: mole concept, atomic structure, thermodynamics, equilibrium
Inorganic: periodic properties, chemical bonding, coordination
Metallurgy, qualitative analysis, p-block and d-block chemistry
Hydrocarbons, functional groups, biomolecules and polymers

syllabus.subject: Mathematics
topics: Algebra: complex numbers, quadratic equations, matrices, probability

timeline.label: Registration
timeline.note: Auto-populated from the JEE Main result for qualifiers.

timeline.label: Exam
timeline.note: Paper 1 in the morning, Paper 2 in the afternoon.

exams.name: National Eligibility cum Entrance Test
exams.fullName: NEET (UG) — MBBS, BDS, AYUSH, BVSc, BSc Nursing and BSMS admissions
exams.about: One offline paper, ~24 lakh candidates and a single rank that decides every medical seat in India. Biology is 50% of the paper.
exams.eligibility: Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Biotechnology and English — 50% aggregate for General, 40% for OBC/SC/ST, 45% for PwBD. Minimum 17 years of age.
exams.attempts: No cap (the earlier 3-attempt limit was removed).

stages.name: NEET (UG)
stages.negative: +4 per correct, −1 per wrong, 0 for unattempted
stages.note: 2026 pattern: 45 questions per subject, all compulsory — no optional questions.

stages.name: Counselling
stages.note: 15% AIQ through MCC, 85% state quota through state authorities.

syllabus.subject: Physics
topics: System of particles and rotational motion
Thermodynamics and kinetic theory of gases
Magnetic effect of current and magnetism
EM induction, alternating current, EM waves
Dual nature of radiation and matter

syllabus.subject: Chemistry
topics: Structure of atom and periodic classification
States of matter: gases and liquids
Redox reactions, hydrogen, s-block and p-block elements
Alcohols, phenols, ethers, aldehydes, ketones, acids
Amines, biomolecules, polymers and chemistry in everyday life

syllabus.subject: Botany
topics: The living world and biological classification
Plant kingdom, morphology and anatomy of flowering plants
Reproduction in organisms and sexual reproduction in plants

syllabus.subject: Zoology
topics: Excretion, locomotion, neural control and coordination
Human health and disease, microbes in human welfare

exams.name: Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering
exams.fullName: GATE — M.Tech/M.E./PhD admissions in IITs & NITs and PSU recruitment
exams.body: IITs and IISc on rotation (GATE Committee)
exams.about: 65 questions, 100 marks, 3 hours — and a score valid for three years. MCQs, multiple-select questions and numerical answers with no choices to guess from.
exams.eligibility: Bachelor's degree in Engineering/Technology/Architecture or Science, or a student in the 3rd year or above of such a programme. No age limit.
exams.attempts: Unlimited.
exams.mode: Computer based test (CBT), virtual calculator provided
exams.website: gate.iisc.ac.in (portal changes with the conducting institute)

stages.name: GATE paper
stages.negative: 1/3 for a 1-mark MCQ, 2/3 for a 2-mark MCQ; none for MSQ and NAT
stages.note: Two sessions across the weekend for most papers.

stages.name: PSU / M.Tech selection
stages.note: GATE score is used for IIT/NIT M.Tech admission, IIT/IISc PhD shortlisting and PSU recruitment.

syllabus.subject: Computer Science & IT
topics: Engineering mathematics: linear algebra, calculus, probability
Theory of computation and compiler design
Operating systems, DBMS and computer networks

syllabus.subject: Mechanical Engineering
topics: Thermodynamics, heat transfer and power engineering

syllabus.subject: Electrical Engineering
topics: Power electronics, analog and digital electronics

syllabus.subject: Civil Engineering
topics: Structural analysis, RCC and steel design

timeline.label: Result & scorecard
timeline.note: Score valid for 3 years.

timeline.label: COAP / PSU recruitment
timeline.note: COAP for IIT admissions, PSU applications through their own portals.

exams.name: Common University Entrance Test (UG)
exams.fullName: CUET (UG) — the single entrance for 260+ central, state and private universities
exams.about: Pick up to 5 subjects: languages, Class-12 domain subjects and the General Test. Each subject is its own short CBT slot, and universities decide which combination they want.
exams.eligibility: Class 12 pass or appearing from any recognised board. No age limit; eligibility criteria vary by university and programme.
exams.attempts: No cap.
exams.mode: Computer based test (CBT), multiple shifts, NTA normalised scores

stages.name: Section IA & IB — Languages
stages.note: IA offers 13 languages, IB offers 20 foreign and additional languages. Attempt any 40 of 50.

stages.name: Section II — Domain subjects
stages.note: 27 domain subjects drawn from the Class 12 NCERT syllabus; up to 4–5 can be chosen.

sections.name: Legal Studies, Psychology, Computer Science, Fine Arts and more

stages.name: Section III — General Test
stages.note: Attempt any 50 of 60. Required for most general and interdisciplinary programmes.

stages.name: University merit lists
stages.note: Universities convert NTA scores into their own merit lists and run their own counselling.

syllabus.subject: Language test (Section IA)
topics: Reading comprehension — factual, literary and narrative passages
Grammar: tenses, voice, narration, parts of speech

syllabus.subject: Accountancy
topics: Accounting for partnership firms and companies
Share capital, debentures and financial statements
Analysis of financial statements, ratios and cash flow

syllabus.subject: Physics / Chemistry / Mathematics / Biology
topics: Full Class 12 NCERT syllabus of the chosen science subject

syllabus.subject: History / Political Science / Geography / Sociology
topics: Full Class 12 NCERT syllabus of the chosen humanities subject

timeline.label: Application window
timeline.note: Choose languages, domain subjects and cities carefully — corrections are limited.

exams.name: Common University Entrance Test (PG)
exams.fullName: CUET (PG) — admission to MA, MSc, MCom, LLM, M.Tech and other PG programmes
exams.about: A domain-based PG entrance used by central universities. Part A tests general awareness and reasoning; Part B tests your undergraduate discipline.
exams.eligibility: Bachelor's degree (or final-year students) in the relevant discipline, as specified by each university.
exams.attempts: No cap.

stages.name: CUET PG test
stages.note: Part A (General Test) is common to all; Part B is the domain paper you choose.

syllabus.subject: Part B — Domain paper
topics: Core undergraduate syllabus of your chosen discipline
Commerce, economics, sciences, humanities, law, education, arts
Check the university-specific CO-PO / test paper code

exams.name: National Eligibility Test
exams.fullName: UGC-NET — eligibility for Assistant Professor and Junior Research Fellowship in 84 subjects
exams.body: National Testing Agency (NTA) on behalf of UGC
exams.about: Paper 1 is common; Paper 2 is your post-graduation subject. No negative marking, and a JRF qualification opens funded PhD routes.
exams.eligibility: Master's degree with 55% (50% for reserved categories). Final-year PG students may apply. JRF has an age limit (usually 30 years, relaxations apply); Assistant Professor has no age limit.
exams.attempts: No cap for Assistant Professor; JRF is limited by the age window.

stages.name: Paper 1 — General
stages.note: Teaching and research aptitude, common to every subject.

stages.name: Paper 2 — Subject
stages.note: Both papers run back-to-back in one 3-hour session.

syllabus.subject: Paper 1 — Teaching & Research Aptitude
topics: Research aptitude: types, methods, ethics and Positivism
Data interpretation and ICT in teaching
Higher education system: governance, policies, institutions

syllabus.subject: Paper 2 — your PG subject
topics: Complete post-graduation syllabus of the chosen subject
84 subjects from Commerce to Computer Science to Languages
Unit-wise coverage from the official UGC syllabus
Previous year papers and NTA-style questions

exams.name: Central Teacher Eligibility Test
exams.fullName: CTET — eligibility to teach Classes I–V (Paper I) and VI–VIII (Paper II) in CBSE and most state schools
exams.about: An eligibility test, not a recruitment test: 60% (55% for reserved categories) makes you eligible, and the certificate is used with state and central school recruitment drives.
exams.eligibility: Paper I: Senior Secondary with 50% and a D.El.Ed / B.El.Ed / 4-year B.A.El.Ed, or graduation with a 2-year Diploma in Education. Paper II: graduation plus B.Ed or D.El.Ed as applicable.
exams.attempts: Unlimited; there is no attempt cap.

stages.name: Paper I — Classes I to V
Paper II — Classes VI to VIII

Learning and pedagogy: motivation, memory, thinking
Assessment for learning vs assessment of learning, CCE

Challenges of language teaching in diverse classrooms

syllabus.subject: Mathematics (Paper I) / Maths & Science (Paper II)
topics: Number system, geometry, mensuration and data handling
Pedagogy: nature of mathematics, error analysis
Science (Paper II): food, materials, natural phenomena

syllabus.subject: Environmental Studies (Paper I)
topics: Family, friends, food, shelter, water, travel
Integration of EVS concepts across subjects

syllabus.subject: Social Studies / Social Science (Paper II)
topics: History, geography and political science basics
Social life and the contemporary world
